title: ROS 2 Fundamentals Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of ROS 2 core concepts, nodes, topics, and services

questions.question: What does ROS stand for?
questions.explanation: ROS (Robot Operating System) is a flexible framework for writing robot software.

questions.question: In ROS 2, what is a node?
questions.explanation: A node is a process that performs computation. Nodes are connected via ROS communication infrastructure.

questions.question: What is a topic in ROS?
questions.explanation: Topics implement a publish-subscribe pattern where publishers send data and subscribers receive it asynchronously.

questions.question: What is the key difference between a topic and a service in ROS?
options: Topics are synchronous, services are asynchronous
Topics are publish-subscribe, services are request-reply
questions.explanation: Topics use publish-subscribe (asynchronous), while services use request-reply (synchronous) communication.

questions.question: What is a subscriber in ROS?
options: A process that receives messages from a topic
questions.explanation: A subscriber is a process that receives messages published to a topic.

questions.question: ROS 2 is a real-time operating system.
questions.explanation: ROS 2 provides tools for robotics but is not a real-time OS itself. It can run on real-time systems.

questions.question: What is the DDS (Data Distribution Service) in ROS 2?
options: The middleware layer that handles communication between nodes
questions.explanation: DDS is the middleware standard that ROS 2 uses for inter-process communication.

questions.question: What are message types in ROS?
options: Data structures that define the content of messages
questions.explanation: Message types are data structures that define the format of data communicated between nodes.

questions.question: In ROS 2, multiple subscribers can receive data from the same topic.
questions.explanation: Yes, the publish-subscribe model allows multiple subscribers to receive data from one publisher topic.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the ROS parameter server?
options: To store and provide runtime configuration parameters
questions.explanation: The parameter server is a centralized store for runtime configuration parameters that nodes can access.
